s: a food hall inside a restored Grade II-listed Victorian market hall
w: Manchester's old Smithfield Market building, a Grade II-listed Victorian hall, reopened as a relaxed food hall of independent vendors under communal tables -- honest pizza, tacos and more served beneath the original iron and glass. Post-industrial rebirth without the tourist gloss, and busy with locals rather than a coach-trip crowd.
_facts: Located at Smithfield Market Hall, 1 Eagle Street, Manchester M4 5BU, Northern Quarter
Housed in a Grade II-listed former Victorian market building
Food hall format with multiple independent food and drink vendors under one roof
Sister venue to Kirkgate Market in Leeds and Mackie Mayor's original Manchester concept

s: an industrial-chic café-bar softened by a wall of hanging plants
w: A café-bar on Tib Street in the Smithfield Buildings, all big windows, high ceilings and exposed industrial bones softened by a wall of hanging plants. Good coffee, a short but well-judged menu, and a relaxed crowd of Northern Quarter regulars rather than passing tourists.
_facts: Located at Smithfield Building, 44 Tib Street, Manchester M4 1NB, Northern Quarter
Café-bar known for industrial decor softened by a large hanging-plant wall
Serves coffee, cocktails and a limited food menu

s: a speakeasy-style bar hidden behind an unmarked shop window
w: A cocktail bar disguised behind a nondescript shop window on Stevenson Square -- easy to walk past unless you're told to look for it. Vintage furniture, a proper back-room speakeasy feel, and careful cocktails, in the kind of low-key reveal that Northern Quarter regulars keep half to themselves.
_facts: Located at Sevendale House, Stevenson Square, Manchester M1 1DN, Northern Quarter
Speakeasy-style cocktail bar accessed through an unmarked shop-front entrance
Known for vintage interior styling and a hidden, discovery-based entrance

a: Manchester Craft and Design Centre, Northern Quarter
s: a brunch café tucked inside a restored Victorian fish-and-poultry market turned artist studios
w: A café inside the Manchester Craft and Design Centre -- a restored Victorian fish and poultry market now given over to working artist studios -- serving brunch to a mix of makers and in-the-know locals. Industrial ironwork overhead, contemporary craft on every side, and a genuinely hidden-feeling stop even in the middle of the Northern Quarter.
_facts: Located at 17 Oak Street, Manchester M4 5JD, inside the Manchester Craft and Design Centre
The Craft and Design Centre building is a restored Victorian fish and poultry market, now home to artist studios
Café known for brunch and a relaxed, creative-community atmosphere
